title: Reply to Comment on “The Current State of Undergraduate Hydrology Courses in North America: A Path Forward”
content:
Abstract

We thank the authors of Hong et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025WR041736) for their thoughtful comments, as well as the opportunity for continued discourse related to undergraduate hydrology education. In our Reply, we consider and respond to the points raised by Hong et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025WR041736), namely at what level convergence should be sought in an undergraduate hydrology course. While we agree with Hong et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025WR041736) that introductory hydrology courses need not be uniform, we still posit that there is value in greater community discourse on learning objectives, content, and approaches to undergraduate hydrology coursework. Above all, we hope that Kelleher et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025wr041736) provides a source of inspiration for hydrology educators, and, with thanks to Hong et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025WR041736) for embracing the opportunity to continue the conversation, spurs future community discussion and engagement on this important topic.
